senses.def: to shout loudly to show support, joy, or praise
examples: The crowd cheered as the runners crossed the finish line.
Fans cheered for the home team all night.

senses.def: to make someone feel happier (cheer up)
examples: I bought her flowers to cheer her up.

senses.def: a shout of joy, support, or praise
examples: A loud cheer went up when the band came on stage.

note: "Cheers!" is said when drinking together (şerefe). In British English it also means "thanks" or "bye".

senses.def: happy and showing it in the way you behave
examples: She's always cheerful, even early in the morning.
The waiter greeted us with a cheerful smile.

senses.def: bright and pleasant, making you feel happy
examples: They painted the kids' room a cheerful yellow.

senses.def: a food made from milk, which can be soft or hard
examples: I'd like a ham and cheese sandwich, please.
Sprinkle some grated cheese on top of the pasta.

note: Photographers say "Say cheese!" to make people smile. "Cheesy" informally means cheap or too sentimental.

senses.def: a professional cook, especially the main cook in a restaurant
examples: The chef came out to ask how we liked the meal.
He trained as a chef in Paris.

note: Pronounced /ʃef/ with "sh". "Chef" in English means only a cook, never a boss in general.

senses.def: a substance made by or used in a chemical process
examples: Farmers are using fewer chemicals on their crops.
Store household chemicals out of children's reach.

senses.def: connected with chemistry or produced by chemistry
examples: Rust is the result of a chemical reaction between iron and oxygen.

senses.def: the science that studies substances and how they react with each other
examples: She's majoring in chemistry and plans to go to medical school.
We have a chemistry test on Friday.

senses.def: a natural attraction or understanding between people
examples: The two lead actors have great chemistry on screen.

senses.def: the upper front part of the body between the neck and the stomach
examples: He went to the hospital complaining of chest pains.
She folded her arms across her chest.

senses.def: a large strong box for storing things
examples: We found old letters in a wooden chest in the attic.

note: "Get something off your chest" means tell someone about something that has been worrying you.

senses.def: a bird kept on farms for its eggs and meat
examples: My grandparents keep chickens in their backyard.

senses.def: the meat of this bird
examples: We had roast chicken and potatoes for dinner.

senses.def: (informal) afraid to do something
examples: Don't be chicken, just jump in the water!

note: "Chicken out" means decide not to do something because you are scared.

senses.def: the person with the highest rank in an organization or group
examples: The police chief held a press conference this morning.
She was promoted to chief of surgery.

senses.def: most important; main
examples: Cost was our chief concern when choosing a school.
He is the company's chief financial officer.

note: "Chiefly" means mainly: The book is chiefly about her childhood.

senses.def: a young person who is not yet an adult
examples: The museum is free for children under twelve.
As a child, I spent every summer at my grandparents' house.

senses.def: a son or daughter of any age
examples: They have three grown children who live in different states.

note: Irregular plural: children. "Childish" is negative (immature); "childlike" is positive (innocent).

senses.def: the time of someone's life when they are a child
examples: She had a happy childhood on a farm in Ohio.
Reading was my favorite hobby in childhood.

senses.def: (American) a thin, crisp slice of fried potato sold in bags
examples: We ate a whole bag of chips while watching the game.

senses.def: (British) a long piece of fried potato
examples: In London, we ordered fish and chips at a pub.

senses.def: a very small piece of electronic material that makes a computer work
examples: A shortage of computer chips slowed car production.

senses.def: a small piece broken off something, or the mark left
examples: There's a chip in this mug, so I'll throw it away.

note: American chips = British crisps; British chips = American French fries. "Chip in" means contribute money.

senses.def: a sweet brown food made from cocoa beans
examples: I bought a bar of dark chocolate.
She gave me a box of chocolates for my birthday.

senses.def: a hot drink made with chocolate and milk
examples: The kids drank hot chocolate after playing in the snow.

note: Usually two syllables in American speech: /ˈtʃɔːklət/. "Chocolates" (plural) are individual pieces in a box.

senses.def: the act of choosing between possibilities, or the thing chosen
examples: Moving to Seattle was the right choice for our family.
We had no choice but to cancel the trip.

senses.def: the range of things you can choose from
examples: The menu offers a wide choice of vegetarian dishes.

note: "Have no choice but to" + verb: We had no choice but to wait. Say "make a choice", not "do a choice".

senses.def: a group of people who sing together, often in church or school
examples: She has sung in the church choir since she was ten.
The school choir performed at the holiday concert.

note: Pronounced /ˈkwaɪər/, like "quire". "Preach to the choir" means try to convince people who already agree with you.

senses.def: to decide which thing or person you want from a group
examples: It's hard to choose a good restaurant in a new city.
You can choose between chicken and fish.

senses.tr: (bir şeyi yapmaya) karar vermek, tercih etmek
senses.def: to decide to do something
examples: Many graduates choose to stay in the city where they studied.

note: Irregular verb: choose – chose – chosen. Don't confuse "choose" /tʃuːz/ with "chose" /tʃoʊz/.

senses.def: to cut something into pieces with a knife or other sharp tool
examples: Chop the onions and garlic finely.
He chopped wood for the fireplace.

senses.def: a thick slice of meat with a bone in it
examples: We grilled pork chops for dinner.

note: "Chopper" is also informal for a helicopter.

senses.def: (of an illness or problem) lasting a long time and hard to cure
examples: She has suffered from chronic back pain for years.
The country faces a chronic shortage of nurses.

note: Opposite: acute (sudden and severe). "Chronically ill" means having a long-term illness.

senses.def: a thick, solid piece of something
examples: Add chunks of pineapple to the salad.
A chunk of ice fell from the roof.

senses.def: (informal) a large part or amount of something
examples: Rent takes a big chunk of my paycheck.

senses.def: a building where Christians go to worship
examples: The old church in the town square was built in 1850.
They got married in a small church by the lake.

senses.def: religious services held in a church
examples: My grandparents go to church every Sunday.

note: No article for the activity: "go to church". "Separation of church and state" is a key US principle.

senses.def: a thin paper tube filled with tobacco, for smoking
examples: He quit smoking cigarettes after his heart attack.
Cigarette butts littered the sidewalk.

note: In American English the stress is often on the first syllable: CIG-a-rette.

senses.def: (mainly British) a building where movies are shown
examples: The new cinema downtown has reclining seats.

senses.def: movies as an art or industry
examples: She's an expert on Iranian cinema.
The festival celebrates independent cinema.

note: Americans usually say "movie theater" for the building and "go to the movies"; "cinema" is more for film as an art.

senses.def: a perfectly round shape, or things arranged in this shape
examples: The children sat in a circle around the teacher.
Draw a circle in the middle of the page.

senses.def: a group of people with shared interests or connections
examples: She has a small circle of close friends.
The idea is popular in academic circles.

senses.def: to draw a circle around something, or to move around something
examples: Circle the correct answer.
The plane circled the airport for half an hour.

note: "Come full circle" = return to the starting point. "Vicious circle" (kısır döngü) = one problem causing another.

senses.def: the complete path that an electric current flows around
examples: A short circuit caused the fire in the kitchen.
Engineers designed a new circuit for the device.

senses.def: a route or track that goes around a place and back to the start
examples: The runners completed three circuits of the park.

senses.def: a regular series of events or places visited by performers or players
examples: After the book came out, she joined the lecture circuit.

note: The "ui" is pronounced /ɪ/: SUR-kit.

senses.def: (of liquid or air) to move continuously around a system or space
examples: Blood circulates through the body.
Open the windows to let air circulate.

senses.def: to spread from person to person, or to send a document to many people
examples: Rumors circulated that the CEO would resign.
The agenda was circulated before the meeting.

senses.def: the movement of blood around the body
examples: Regular exercise improves circulation.
Poor circulation can make your hands and feet cold.

senses.def: the number of copies of a newspaper sold, or the use of money or ideas among people
examples: The newspaper's circulation has fallen by half.
The old coins were taken out of circulation.

senses.def: a fact or condition that affects a situation (usually plural)
examples: Under the circumstances, we decided to postpone the wedding.
He died in mysterious circumstances.

senses.def: the financial or living conditions of a person
examples: The scholarship helps students from difficult circumstances.

note: Use "under/in the circumstances". "Circumstantial evidence" suggests guilt without directly proving it.

senses.def: to mention something as a reason or example
examples: She cited family reasons for leaving the job.
The report cites rising costs as the main problem.

senses.def: to refer to a book, article, or author as evidence
examples: Make sure you cite all your sources in the essay.

note: Same pronunciation as "site" and "sight". Academic papers are judged partly by how often they are cited.

senses.def: a person who has the legal right to live in a country
examples: She became a US citizen after ten years in the country.
All citizens over eighteen have the right to vote.

senses.def: a person who lives in a particular town or city
examples: The mayor met with concerned citizens about the new highway.

note: A "senior citizen" is an older person, usually retired.

senses.def: the legal right to belong to a country
examples: He applied for Canadian citizenship last year.
She holds dual citizenship.

senses.def: the duties and behavior expected of a member of a community
examples: The school teaches good citizenship through volunteer work.

senses.def: a large and important town
examples: New York is the largest city in the United States.
We moved from the city to a small town.

note: "City hall" is the building of local government. "Inner city" suggests poor central areas.

senses.def: connected with a city or with the duties of citizens
examples: Voting is a basic civic duty.
Local leaders are trying to increase civic engagement.

note: "Civics" is a school subject about citizens' rights and the government.

senses.def: connected with the people of a country and their rights, not the military or religion
examples: The country was torn apart by civil war.
The movement fought for civil rights in the 1960s.

senses.def: relating to private legal cases, not criminal ones
examples: The family filed a civil lawsuit against the company.

senses.def: polite but not very friendly
examples: Even after the divorce, they stayed civil to each other.

note: "Civil" usually means "related to citizens". For "not military" people, use "civilian": civilian casualties, not "civil casualties".

senses.def: a person who is not in the armed forces or the police
examples: Thousands of civilians fled the city as the fighting grew worse.
The bombing killed both soldiers and civilians.

senses.def: connected with people who are not in the armed forces
examples: After twenty years in the army, he struggled to adjust to civilian life.

senses.def: a highly developed society with its own culture and way of life
examples: Ancient Egyptian civilization lasted for thousands of years.
The museum explores the great civilizations of the Americas.

senses.def: (humorous) a place with modern comforts, especially a town
examples: After a week of camping, we were glad to get back to civilization.

note: British spelling: civilisation. "Civilized" also means polite and reasonable.

senses.def: to say something is true, although it has not been proved
examples: The company claims that its product is completely safe.
He claims to have met the president.

senses.def: to ask for something because you believe you have a right to it
examples: You can claim your bags at carousel number four.
Nobody has claimed the lost wallet.

senses.def: a statement that something is true without proof
examples: Scientists have rejected claims that the vaccine is unsafe.

senses.def: a formal request for money you think you are owed
examples: She filed an insurance claim after the accident.

note: "Claim" suggests doubt about whether it's true. "Claim lives" means cause deaths: The flood claimed ten lives.

senses.def: to make something clearer or easier to understand
examples: Could you clarify what you mean by "soon"?
The new guidelines clarify who is responsible for safety.

note: Past form: clarified. "Ask for clarification" is a polite way to say "I don't understand".

senses.def: the quality of being clear and easy to understand, see, or hear
examples: The teacher praised the clarity of her writing.
We need more clarity about the new rules.

senses.def: a short fight between two groups
examples: There were violent clashes between police and protesters.

senses.def: a serious disagreement
examples: The meeting ended in a clash over the budget.

senses.def: to fight or argue; (of colors or styles) to look bad together
examples: Protesters clashed with police outside parliament.
That red tie clashes with your orange shirt.

note: Events can also "clash" when they happen at the same time: The two meetings clash.

senses.def: a group of students taught together
examples: There are thirty students in my class.

senses.def: a period of time when students are taught
examples: I have a chemistry class at nine.
She takes yoga classes twice a week.

senses.def: a social group with a similar level of money, education, or status
examples: The tax cuts mostly helped the middle class.

senses.def: a level of quality or service, for example on a plane
examples: We flew business class to Tokyo.

note: The room is a "classroom", not a "class". "The class of 2025" means students who graduate that year.

senses.def: considered one of the best of its kind and admired for a long time
examples: Casablanca is a classic Hollywood film.
They drove a classic 1960s convertible.

senses.def: a very typical example of something
examples: Forgetting his keys again was a classic mistake.

senses.def: a book, film, or song that is well known and admired as excellent
examples: Everyone should read some of the classics of American literature.

note: "Classic" = typical or of lasting quality; "classical" = traditional, ancient, or serious music.

senses.def: related to serious, traditional Western music
examples: She plays classical piano and loves Bach.
The radio station plays classical music all night.

senses.def: connected with ancient Greece and Rome
examples: The building's design was inspired by classical architecture.

senses.def: traditional and widely accepted in style or form
examples: The book uses a classical approach to economics.

note: Say "classical music", not "classic music".

senses.def: the act or system of putting people or things into groups
examples: The classification of plants is based on their features.
Films receive an age classification before release.

senses.def: to arrange people or things in groups based on shared features
examples: Libraries classify books by subject.
The storm was classified as a category 4 hurricane.

senses.def: to officially make information secret
examples: The documents were classified for national security reasons.

note: "Classified ads" are small newspaper or online ads for jobs, cars, etc.

senses.def: a room where a class of students is taught
examples: The classroom was empty when I arrived.
Every classroom now has a smart board.

note: Turkish "sınıf" covers both the room (classroom) and the students (class).

senses.def: a separate section of a legal document
examples: The contract includes a clause about early termination.
Read the confidentiality clause carefully before you sign.

senses.def: a group of words with a subject and a verb
examples: "Because it was raining" is a dependent clause.

note: Pronounced like "claws".

senses.def: not dirty
examples: Put on a clean shirt before dinner.
The hotel room was clean and quiet.

senses.def: not involving anything illegal or dishonest; not harmful to the environment
examples: The country is investing heavily in clean energy.
He has a clean driving record.

senses.def: to remove dirt or dust from something
examples: I spent all Saturday cleaning the house.

note: "Come clean" means confess the truth. "Make a clean break" means end something completely.

senses.def: easy to understand, see, or hear; without doubt
examples: The instructions were clear and simple.
It's clear that she's not happy with the decision.

senses.def: easy to see through; without clouds
examples: The water was so clear we could see the fish.
On a clear day, you can see the mountains.

senses.def: to remove things or people that are not wanted from a place
examples: Workers cleared the snow from the road.
Can you help me clear the table?

senses.def: to prove someone is not guilty, or to give official permission
examples: The court cleared him of all charges.

note: "Steer clear of" means avoid. "Clear up" can mean explain a misunderstanding or the weather getting better.

senses.def: in a way that is easy to see, hear, or understand
examples: Please speak clearly into the microphone.
The sign was clearly visible from the road.

senses.def: used to say that something is obvious
examples: Clearly, the plan isn't working.
She was clearly upset about the news.

senses.def: (American) a person who serves customers in a store or hotel
examples: The clerk at the front desk gave us our room keys.
Ask the store clerk if they have it in a smaller size.

senses.def: a person who keeps records or does office work
examples: She worked as a court clerk for ten years.

note: American pronunciation /klɜːrk/ rhymes with "work"; British is /klɑːk/.
